status: bounded-research-complete; production lifetime proof remains open

findings.claim: 3A7A40 encloses the early Actor+1472 zero and later current-player/STATUS publication in the captured playable constructor family.
findings.limit: A wrapper around 3B3200 returns before the nonnull binding. Birth notification follows the first zero store. The STATUS allocator returns before both backlink stores. The constructor's transitive no-yield and callback-lock properties are not proved.

findings.claim: Normal spawn and Drive replacement reach 405030 then 3A7A40. Alternate playable constructors also reach 3A7A40.
findings.limit: A 3DF930 gate misses Drive replacement; a 405030 gate misses other constructors. Tail jumps remove dispatcher frames, so bootstrap cannot depend only on finding the outer dispatcher frame.

findings.claim: 415670 and the inlined specialization in 4158C0 both call 3A7A40. The recorded rescue task path reaches 4158C0.
findings.limit: 415670 has no returned direct code caller, which does not exclude indirect calls. Gating only 3A7A40 misses earlier current-player parking in 4158C0.

findings.claim: The Drive replacement task contains cooperative wait calls before and after construction.
findings.limit: Task and yield semantics additionally use the prior verified scheduler study. Registration proves no universal OS-thread affinity. A lock cannot safely span this whole cooperative task.

findings.claim: 3BF300 first destroys pending actors through virtual callbacks, then moves marked actors from the active list to the pending list. Cleanup callback 3BF4C0 invokes this pass twice.
findings.limit: This explains deferred deletion; it does not prove every actor allocation reaches a virtual destructor or exclude bulk heap release. Native work also precedes the virtual destruction callback.

findings.claim: 41EA20 has a candidate mutex region around its 3DF930 call.
findings.limit: The 20-body scope excludes full mutex helper bodies and import resolution. Eleven other direct 3DF930 callers remain. This is no proof of shared mutual exclusion.

priorEvidence.scope: Previously verified scheduler 14EB70 → 14FC20 → 14FD60 invokes tasks or cooperative fibers; returning from update does not join every OS thread. Motion batches wait via 130130; resource worker 3A0C60 is separate.

Previously verified possible motion-worker path reaches the BDX VM through 3BF4E0, 3BFAB0, 3C6AA0, 3B5E80, 3E1840, 3E1C80 and 41B400. No shipped event-27 asset reaching these constructors was identified in this round.

Pin holds metadata only. Separate Resolve/Pin creates a TOCTOU interval. The death observer releases its Actor lock before forwarding native code; holding that lock across native STATUS operations would conflict with STATUS-to-Actor metadata ordering.

recommendation: Treat 3A7A40 as an earlier observation candidate for this constructor family, with no claim of a universal lifetime boundary.
Before native binding mutations, prevent transaction admission until the operation finishes. Bootstrap must drain earlier calls, including tail-call and parked-fiber cases.
Keep STATUS-to-Actor metadata ordering for a short guard across validation and commit. Do not hold that metadata lock over entire native constructors or the Drive task.
PoolOwns, backlinks and ActorGeneration cannot substitute for native allocation lifetime. Prove coverage of bulk frees, rebinds and current-player transitions.
Keep production provider/STATUS activation unavailable until coverage and bootstrap are established.
